title: The Collapse at Netflix Signals the End of Audience Capture
excerpt: The most popular strategy in the tech world has stopped working. That's good news for all of us.
content_html:
Today’s culture briefing is free for everyone. Enjoy!

If you value analysis of this sort, consider taking out a premium subscription.

A few weeks ago, I warned about problems brewing at Netflix (and other streaming platforms). In just the last few days, these problems have gotten worse, much worse—and the situation has reached crisis proportions.

Even more revealing—the crisis is now spreading through the tech world like a wildfire. It’s no exaggeration to say that Netflix dragged down the entire NASDAQ today, after the release of its disappointing quarterly results.

That’s because savvy investors on Wall Street now grasp what’s really going on. They fear that the root cause of Netflix’s woes portends the collapse of the dominant business strategy in tech today.

This is hugely important—and not just for investors or technocrats. All of us will be impacted by how this plays out. And I have a strong hunch that what is bad for Netflix might just be good for you and me.

That’s because Netflix’s failed strategy is audience capture. And you and I are part of the audience it wants to keep in captivity.

More on that below—but let’s start by looking at the damage done to Netflix’s stock. When I warned about it in June, the price had already dropped 45%.

But today, shareholders woke up to this.

After today’s debacle, Netflix will have wiped out the entire last two years of stock price gains.

This is usually where I take a victory lap, and point out that I warned of the danger three weeks ago. But there’s a bigger story here that must be told.

The disappointing earnings call yesterday is just the tip of the iceberg. The company’s reluctance to provide viewership numbers is an even more revealing sign of how bad things really are.

Netflix once bragged regularly about its growing user base. But yesterday they refused to share updated viewership numbers until 2027!

Yet even without those metrics, you can see evidence of a coming corporate collapse—but only if you dig deeply into the numbers.

Last week, for example, we learned that Netflix’s audience is skipping the second season of the platform’s hottest offerings.

That’s scary stuff for Netflix. But it gets worse. The audience is also losing interest in the platform’s brand new series.

The situation is so dire that even Netflix’s biggest new series of the second quarter failed to get renewed. But if the platform can’t count on its new hits, will anything save it?

Netflix doesn’t want to tell us about users canceling their subscriptions. But just go over to Reddit and other platforms where people say what they really think about the company. You will get an earful.

This is typical:

Funny I was talking to my wife about how Netflix has practically nothing left we want to watch and maybe it was time to move on. If this price increase goes through that would be the final straw. I suspect a lot of others are getting close to that limit….

Another frustrated customer didn’t even make a comment—just shared some numbers. But the figures paint a dismal picture.

Netflix got into this mess by pursuing a simple strategy: (1) Reduce the number of new scripted series (which peaked in 2022), but (2) Raise subscription prices.

That is the “audience capture” strategy mentioned above. The idea is that the audience got captured years ago with cheap subscription prices, and now the platform can squeeze them mercilessly—offering less and charging more. Netflix has been pursuing this agenda for several years now.

Ah, but Netflix isn’t the only company building its future on audience capture. It’s getting used at almost every streaming platform. And even companies outside of the media space are practicing variants of it. You see it at Google, Meta, X, Apple, etc.

It’s shocking how many companies have learned this technique. The entire printer and toner business is now built on audience capture. The same is true of the software industry—don’t even get me started on my Microsoft Office subscription fiasco. And, of course, all those customer loyalty programs (variants on the frequent flyer gimmicks that started this craze years ago) are examples of the same stale strategy.

Even the AI world is turning into an audience capture business—both for itself and its customers. This is one of the key reasons for my frequent criticisms of AI slop. It feeds into step one of the strategy outlined above. The companies use AI to reduce the cost of content, thus boosting margins while reducing their dependence on human creators.

Audience capture has always existed, but never to this extent. When I consulted at BCG we called it a milking strategy, where you raised prices and reduced capital investment in a business—which was now your cash cow. You squeeze all the money you can from it, for as long as you can.

But back then we realized that milking only worked in the short term. Eventually you killed the cow. And the risk is the same today with “audience capture”—which is just a new name for that poor old bovine.

Sooner or later, the audience refuses to be held captive. And that’s happening now at Netflix—hence the stock sell-off.

But it’s happening elsewhere too, although few are paying attention. Look at the share price at Spotify or Disney for ther examples.

Did you know that Mark Zuckerberg’s social media empire has stopped growing? In the first quarter, Meta saw a decline in users for the first time in the company’s history.

This is not just a coincidence. Meta is the king of audience capture, and when it starts losing that audience, other tech companies ought to pay attention.

You should expect to see more problems of this sort at audience capture corporations. And that’s bad news for the technocracy, because this manipulative strategy is everywhere. If it stops producing results, they will need to take drastic steps.

But their nightmare is our blessing. That’s because the end of audience capture means tech companies will need to return to serving customers, not holding them in bondage.

They aren’t ready to take that step—not now, at least. Pleasing customers is hard work. Milking cows is a simpler business. But they won’t have a choice. The cattle are finally resisting. They might even stampede!

Moo, moo, moo!

I give the leading audience capture companies 12-18 months at most before the worst consequences of their overreach hit their financial statements. And it may happen even faster.

If they were wise, they would start acting now. But whether they fix the root cause of their audience capture mess now or later, the end result will be the same. That captive audience will find itself liberated.

If I’m right, this may represent the biggest shift in the consumer economy of our time. So check back here for updates—because this will be a bumpy rodeo ride for all parties.

You squeeze all the money you can from it, for as long as you can.

sentences.en: Audience capture has always existed, but never to this extent.
sentences.zh: 吸引观众一直存在，但从未达到如此程度。

sentences.en: When I consulted at BCG we called it a milking strategy, where you raised prices and reduced capital investment in a business—which was now your cash cow.
sentences.zh: 当我在 BCG 进行咨询时，我们将其称为“挤奶策略”，即提高价格并减少企业的资本投资，而企业现在已成为摇钱树。

sentences.en: You squeeze all the money you can from it, for as long as you can.
sentences.zh: 你可以从中榨取所有的钱，只要你能榨干。

blocks.html_en: But back then we realized that milking only worked in the short term. Eventually you killed the cow. And the risk is the same today with “audience capture”—which is just a new name for that poor old bovine.

sentences.en: But back then we realized that milking only worked in the short term.
sentences.zh: 但当时我们意识到挤奶只能在短期内发挥作用。

sentences.en: Eventually you killed the cow.
sentences.zh: 最后你杀了牛。

sentences.en: And the risk is the same today with “audience capture”—which is just a new name for that poor old bovine.
sentences.zh: 今天的风险与“吸引观众”是一样的——这只是那头可怜的老牛的新名字。

blocks.html_en: Sooner or later, the audience refuses to be held captive. And that’s happening now at Netflix—hence the stock sell-off.

sentences.en: Sooner or later, the audience refuses to be held captive.
sentences.zh: 迟早，观众会拒绝被俘虏。

sentences.en: And that’s happening now at Netflix—hence the stock sell-off.
sentences.zh: Netflix 现在正在发生这种情况，因此股票遭到抛售。

blocks.html_en: But it’s happening elsewhere too, although few are paying attention. Look at the share price at Spotify or Disney for ther examples.

sentences.en: But it’s happening elsewhere too, although few are paying attention.
sentences.zh: 但这种情况也发生在其他地方，尽管很少有人关注。

sentences.en: Look at the share price at Spotify or Disney for ther examples.
sentences.zh: 以 Spotify 或迪士尼的股价为例。

blocks.html_en: Did you know that Mark Zuckerberg’s social media empire has stopped growing? In the first quarter, Meta saw a decline in users for the first time in the company’s history.

sentences.en: Did you know that Mark Zuckerberg’s social media empire has stopped growing?
sentences.zh: 您知道马克·扎克伯格的社交媒体帝国已经停止增长吗？

sentences.en: In the first quarter, Meta saw a decline in users for the first time in the company’s history.
sentences.zh: 第一季度，Meta 的用户数量出现公司历史上首次下降。

blocks.html_en: This is not just a coincidence. Meta is the king of audience capture, and when it starts losing that audience, other tech companies ought to pay attention.

sentences.en: This is not just a coincidence.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是巧合。

sentences.en: Meta is the king of audience capture, and when it starts losing that audience, other tech companies ought to pay attention.
sentences.zh: Meta 是吸引受众的王者，当它开始失去受众时，其他科技公司应该引起注意。

blocks.html_en: You should expect to see more problems of this sort at audience capture corporations. And that’s bad news for the technocracy, because this manipulative strategy is everywhere. If it stops producing results, they will need to take drastic steps.

sentences.en: You should expect to see more problems of this sort at audience capture corporations.
sentences.zh: 您应该预计在受众捕获公司中会看到更多此类问题。

sentences.en: And that’s bad news for the technocracy, because this manipulative strategy is everywhere.
sentences.zh: 这对于技术官僚来说是个坏消息，因为这种操纵策略无处不在。

sentences.en: If it stops producing results, they will need to take drastic steps.
sentences.zh: 如果它停止产生结果，他们将需要采取严厉措施。

blocks.html_en: But their nightmare is our blessing. That’s because the end of audience capture means tech companies will need to return to serving customers, not holding them in bondage.

sentences.en: But their nightmare is our blessing.
sentences.zh: 但他们的噩梦是我们的祝福。

sentences.en: That’s because the end of audience capture means tech companies will need to return to serving customers, not holding them in bondage.
sentences.zh: 这是因为受众捕获的结束意味着科技公司将需要回归服务客户，而不是束缚他们。

blocks.html_en: They aren’t ready to take that step—not now, at least. Pleasing customers is hard work. Milking cows is a simpler business. But they won’t have a choice. The cattle are finally resisting. They might even stampede!

sentences.en: They aren’t ready to take that step—not now, at least.
sentences.zh: 他们还没有准备好迈出这一步——至少现在还没有。

sentences.en: Pleasing customers is hard work.
sentences.zh: 取悦客户是一项艰苦的工作。

sentences.en: Milking cows is a simpler business.
sentences.zh: 挤奶是一件更简单的事情。

sentences.en: But they won’t have a choice.
sentences.zh: 但他们别无选择。

sentences.en: The cattle are finally resisting.
sentences.zh: 牛终于反抗了。

sentences.en: They might even stampede!
sentences.zh: 他们甚至可能会发生踩踏事件！

blocks.html_en: Moo, moo, moo!

sentences.en: Moo, moo, moo!
sentences.zh: 哞、哞、哞！

blocks.html_en: I give the leading audience capture companies 12-18 months at most before the worst consequences of their overreach hit their financial statements. And it may happen even faster.

sentences.en: I give the leading audience capture companies 12-18 months at most before the worst consequences of their overreach hit their financial statements.
sentences.zh: 我预计领先的观众捕捉公司最多需要 12 到 18 个月的时间，他们的财务报表就会因过度扩张而产生最严重的后果。

sentences.en: And it may happen even faster.
sentences.zh: 而且它可能发生得更快。

blocks.html_en: If they were wise, they would start acting now. But whether they fix the root cause of their audience capture mess now or later, the end result will be the same. That captive audience will find itself liberated.

sentences.en: If they were wise, they would start acting now.
sentences.zh: 如果他们明智的话，他们现在就会开始行动。

sentences.en: But whether they fix the root cause of their audience capture mess now or later, the end result will be the same.
sentences.zh: 但无论他们现在还是以后解决观众捕捉混乱的根本原因，最终结果都是一样的。

sentences.en: That captive audience will find itself liberated.
sentences.zh: 那些被俘虏的观众将会发现自己获得了解放。

blocks.html_en: If I’m right, this may represent the biggest shift in the consumer economy of our time. So check back here for updates—because this will be a bumpy rodeo ride for all parties.

sentences.en: If I’m right, this may represent the biggest shift in the consumer economy of our time.
sentences.zh: 如果我是对的，这可能代表了我们这个时代消费经济的最大转变。

sentences.en: So check back here for updates—because this will be a bumpy rodeo ride for all parties.
sentences.zh: 因此，请回来查看最新消息，因为这对所有各方来说都将是一次坎坷的牛仔竞技之旅。

content_html_zh:
今天的文化简报对所有人免费。 享受！

如果您重视此类分析，请考虑订阅高级版。

几周前，我警告过 Netflix（和其他流媒体平台）正在酝酿的问题。 就在最近几天，这些问题变得越来越严重，情况已经达到了危机的程度。

更能说明问题的是，这场危机现在正像野火一样在科技界蔓延。 毫不夸张地说，在公布了令人失望的季度业绩后，Netflix 今天拖累了整个纳斯达克市场。

这是因为华尔街精明的投资者现在了解到底发生了什么。 他们担心 Netflix 陷入困境的根本原因预示着当今科技领域主导商业战略的崩溃。

这非常重要——而且不仅仅是对投资者或技术官僚而言。 我们所有人都会受到事态发展的影响。 我有一种强烈的预感，对 Netflix 不利的事情可能对你我有利。

这是因为 Netflix 失败的策略是吸引观众。 你和我都是它想要圈养的观众的一部分。

下面将详细介绍这一点，但让我们首先看看 Netflix 股票受到的损害。 当我在 6 月份发出警告时，价格已经下跌了 45%。

但今天，股东们醒悟了。

在今天的惨败之后，Netflix 将抹去过去两年的全部股价涨幅。

这通常是我庆祝胜利的地方，并指出我三周前警告过危险。 但这里有一个更大的故事必须讲述。

昨天令人失望的财报电话会议只是冰山一角。 该公司不愿提供收视率数字，这更能说明情况到底有多糟糕。

Netflix 曾经经常吹嘘其不断增长的用户群。 但昨天他们拒绝分享 2027 年之前的最新收视率数据！

然而，即使没有这些指标，你也可以看到公司即将崩溃的证据——但前提是你深入研究这些数字。

例如，上周我们了解到 Netflix 的观众正在跳过该平台最热门节目的第二季。

这对 Netflix 来说是可怕的事情。 但情况变得更糟。 观众也对该平台的全新剧集失去了兴趣。

形势如此严峻，就连Netflix第二季度最大的新剧也未能续订。 但如果该平台不能指望新的热门产品，还有什么可以拯救它呢？

Netflix 不想告诉我们用户取消订阅的情况。 但只要访问 Reddit 和其他平台，人们就会说出他们对公司的真实想法。 你会得到一个耳朵。

这是典型的：

有趣的是，我正在和我的妻子谈论 Netflix 几乎没有我们想看的内容，也许是时候继续前进了。 如果这次涨价成功，那将是压垮他们的最后一根稻草。 我怀疑很多其他人正在接近这个极限……

另一位沮丧的客户甚至没有发表评论，只是分享了一些数字。 但数字描绘了一幅惨淡的画面。

Netflix 陷入困境是因为采取了一个简单的策略：(1) 减少新剧本剧集的数量（在 2022 年达到顶峰），但 (2) 提高订阅价格。

这就是上面提到的“受众捕获”策略。 这个想法是，多年前，观众以低廉的订阅价格被俘获，而现在，该平台可以无情地挤压他们——提供更少的内容，收取更高的费用。 Netflix 多年来一直致力于实现这一目标。

啊，但 Netflix 并不是唯一一家将未来建立在吸引观众的公司上。 几乎每个流媒体平台都在使用它。 甚至媒体领域之外的公司也在实践它的变体。 你可以在 Google、Meta、X、Apple 等处看到它。

令人震惊的是有多少公司已经学会了这项技术。 整个打印机和碳粉业务现在都建立在吸引受众的基础上。 软件行业也是如此——更不用说我的 Microsoft Office 订阅惨败了。 当然，所有这些客户忠诚度计划（多年前掀起这股热潮的常旅客花招的变体）都是同样陈旧策略的例子。

甚至人工智能世界也正在变成一个吸引受众的行业——无论是对于它自己还是它的客户。 这也是我经常批评AI失范的关键原因之一。 它融入了上述策略的第一步。 这些公司利用人工智能来降低内容成本，从而提高利润，同时减少对人类创作者的依赖。

吸引观众一直存在，但从未达到如此程度。 当我在 BCG 进行咨询时，我们将其称为“挤奶策略”，即提高价格并减少企业的资本投资，而企业现在已成为摇钱树。 你可以从中榨取所有的钱，只要你能榨干。

但当时我们意识到挤奶只能在短期内发挥作用。 最后你杀了牛。 今天的风险与“吸引观众”是一样的——这只是那头可怜的老牛的新名字。

迟早，观众会拒绝被俘虏。 Netflix 现在正在发生这种情况，因此股票遭到抛售。

但这种情况也发生在其他地方，尽管很少有人关注。 以 Spotify 或迪士尼的股价为例。

您知道马克·扎克伯格的社交媒体帝国已经停止增长吗？ 第一季度，Meta 的用户数量出现公司历史上首次下降。

这不仅仅是巧合。 Meta 是吸引受众的王者，当它开始失去受众时，其他科技公司应该引起注意。

您应该预计在受众捕获公司中会看到更多此类问题。 这对于技术官僚来说是个坏消息，因为这种操纵策略无处不在。 如果它停止产生结果，他们将需要采取严厉措施。

但他们的噩梦是我们的祝福。 这是因为受众捕获的结束意味着科技公司将需要回归服务客户，而不是束缚他们。

他们还没有准备好迈出这一步——至少现在还没有。 取悦客户是一项艰苦的工作。 挤奶是一件更简单的事情。 但他们别无选择。 牛终于反抗了。 他们甚至可能会发生踩踏事件！

哞、哞、哞！

我预计领先的观众捕捉公司最多需要 12 到 18 个月的时间，他们的财务报表就会因过度扩张而产生最严重的后果。 而且它可能发生得更快。

如果他们明智的话，他们现在就会开始行动。 但无论他们现在还是以后解决观众捕捉混乱的根本原因，最终结果都是一样的。 那些被俘虏的观众将会发现自己获得了解放。

如果我是对的，这可能代表了我们这个时代消费经济的最大转变。 因此，请回来查看最新消息，因为这对所有各方来说都将是一次坎坷的牛仔竞技之旅。
